name: Denmark — Danish parties
intro: compare it with Danish political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Denmark: those represented in the parliament (Folketing) and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the parliament (Folketing) after the 2022 election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 179 members.

EL.name: Enhedslisten
EL.priorities: Welfare state, Climate action, Taxing wealth
EL.description: Red–Green Alliance, a socialist and green party with collective leadership, supportive of Ukraine but critical of NATO.

SF.name: Socialistisk Folkeparti
SF.description: Green Left party, the largest Danish party in the 2024 European election, combining welfare, climate policy and firm support for Ukraine.

ALT.name: Alternativet
ALT.priorities: Climate action, Animal welfare, Democratic reform
ALT.description: Green party that wants to move beyond growth as the goal of politics.

S.name: Socialdemokratiet
S.priorities: Welfare state, Reducing immigration, Defence and support for Ukraine, Public healthcare
S.description: Social Democrats of Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, combining a strong welfare state with one of Europe's strictest immigration policies.

RV.name: Radikale Venstre
RV.priorities: Education, Climate action, Deeper European integration
RV.description: Social-liberal party, pro-European and liberal on migration.

Volt.name: Volt Danmark
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

M.name: Moderaterne
M.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Welfare state, Deeper European integration
M.description: Centrist party of former prime minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen, part of the cross-bloc government since 2022.

V.name: Venstre
V.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Farmers and rural areas, Defence and support for Ukraine
V.description: Liberal Party, Denmark's traditional centre-right force, in government with the Social Democrats since 2022.

K.name: Det Konservative Folkeparti
K.priorities: Security and law and order, Lower taxes, Defence and support for Ukraine
K.description: Conservative People's Party, liberal-conservative and strongly pro-NATO.

LA.name: Liberal Alliance
LA.priorities: Lower taxes, Less red tape, Education
LA.description: Classical-liberal party popular with young voters, calling for much lower taxes and a smaller state.

DD.name: Danmarksdemokraterne
DD.priorities: Reducing immigration, Regions and rural services, Security and law and order
DD.description: Denmark Democrats of Inger Støjberg, a right-wing party focused on rural Denmark and strict immigration.

DF.name: Dansk Folkeparti
DF.priorities: Reducing immigration, Welfare state, National identity
DF.description: Danish People's Party, nationalist and anti-immigration, combining welfare for older people with Euroscepticism.
